subject: Hospitality
title: Upselling Without Alienating
description: A micro-lesson that makes Upselling Without Alienating usable.

hook.text: A well-timed suggestion—'Would you like truffle shavings on that?'—can add $15 to a check.

buildup.text: Effective upselling focuses on enhancing the guest experience, not inflating the bill.

discovery.text: Servers trained in suggestive selling boost average checks by 15–25%. The key is reading the table and matching the guest's mood.

twist.text: Over-upselling creates backlash. Guests who feel pressured tip less, leave negative reviews, and don't return.

climax.text: The best upsell feels natural: genuine enthusiasm about the chef's special converts through passion, not pressure.

punchline.text: Suggest, don't push. The best upsell sounds like friendly advice from a food lover.

quiz.question: By how much can trained suggestive selling increase average checks?
